findings.finding: The canary's leg (ii) fetches historical windows DIRECTLY from Binance outside any limiter: the machine-wide budget in S5 governs gateway-originated requests only, and the canary is a separate process. On the already-banned shared Cloudflare-WARP egress IP this unpaced direct leg can itself re-trigger 418/429 and starve the live PROSPECTIVE-SHADOW-V1 / XAUUSD-SHADOW-V1 workers, contradicting the S9.2 requirement of 'zero worker interference'. Weight seen in X-MBX-USED-WEIGHT-1M is IP-scoped and includes foreign tenants, so the gateway budget cannot bound the canary's direct leg.
findings.remediation_hint: Require the canary direct-Binance leg to run under the same pacing/breaker law (min-gap + bounded attempts + 418/429 hard stop) or route it through the gateway budget; freeze the canary's max request rate in S9.2 before the run.

findings.section: 5 (Rate limiter + circuit breaker) with motivation from 2
findings.finding: Breaker law classifies only 418/429 (open breaker) and 5xx (bounded retry, 3 consecutive => DEGRADED). Live evidence already shows the failure class drifting: the current valuation heartbeat last_error is 'HTTP Error 403: Forbidden' (07:25Z), not 418. Handling of non-retryable 4xx (403/451) is unspecified: as written such a status could either consume the generic <=4 transport-retry budget per logical call or pass untyped, neither of which is a defined breaker/status outcome.
findings.remediation_hint: Add an explicit response-classification law in S5: non-retryable 4xx (403/451/404...) fail fast with a distinct event and no retry consumption; breaker law stays 418/429-scoped.

findings.finding: The 5xx branch retries <=2 'without opening the ban breaker' but does not state whether a Retry-After header on a 5xx response is honored. The owner hard stop 'no Binance retry inside an active Retry-After window' (S15) is not qualified by status class, so a 503 with Retry-After would currently be retried inside its window in the plan as written.
findings.remediation_hint: State that ANY response carrying Retry-After (any status class) suppresses retries until expiry; only then apply the 5xx bounded-retry budget.

findings.finding: Vocabulary mismatch with no defined mapping: S5 mandates the 7 owner-verbatim per-surface states (HEALTHY/DEGRADED/RATE_LIMITED/DISCONNECTED/STALE/GAP_DETECTED/RECOVERING); the S6 per-datum status enum is HEALTHY|STALE|GAP_DETECTED|RATE_LIMITED|DISCONNECTED|NOT_SUBSCRIBED - it omits DEGRADED and RECOVERING and adds NOT_SUBSCRIBED. A consumer reading a single datum cannot see DEGRADED/RECOVERING, and no rule says which datum status a RECOVERING surface reports.
findings.remediation_hint: Define the surface-state -> datum-status mapping in S6 (or extend the datum enum), so per-datum status is total over all 7 surface states.

findings.finding: Over-generalized incident start: 2026-09-21T03:55Z is the ledger-first DATA_BLOCKED mark for ILLIQ-AMIHUD-28D-W and matches the ops-commit outage start (99e00263: 'outage began 03:55Z'), but XSECT-FUND-CARRY-7D carries 23 DATA_BLOCKED marks predating it (first 2026-09-15T16:30Z). The plan sentence applies 'first ~03:55Z' to both ledgers; strictly false for XSECT. The 45/22 counts themselves were exact at plan-commit instant (ledgers now 47/24 after +2 blocked loops, consistent drift).
findings.remediation_hint: Scope 'first ~03:55Z' to the 2026-09-21 outage episode per ops commit 99e00263 and state per-family ledger-firsts (ILLIQ 03:55Z; XSECT has earlier blocked marks from 2026-09-15T16:30Z).

findings.finding: Internal path inconsistency: S13 places the LaunchAgent template under 'research/live_data_gateway/launchagent/' while the frozen code root is 'research/live_gateway/' (S3, S11 module research.live_gateway, S16). Two different committed-code locations for one cycle.
findings.remediation_hint: Unify to one module path (e.g. research/live_gateway/launchagent/) across S3/S11/S13/S16.

findings.finding: Two-tier weight thresholds 'tracked X-MBX-USED-WEIGHT-1M <= 1200 (hard stop-issuing above 1800)' read as a contradiction without a soft-budget vs hard-stop label; also the header measures IP-level weight including foreign tenants the gateway cannot control (relevant on the shared WARP egress), which the text does not acknowledge.
findings.remediation_hint: Label 1200 as soft budget (stop issuing new non-essential requests) and 1800 as hard stop; note shared-IP weight includes foreign traffic and the 418/429 breaker is the compensating control.

findings.finding: Closed-range klines/basis/funding TTL is 'forever' yet the cache store is LRU-capped at 500 MiB; eviction of an immutable range legitimately causes re-download, but the plan only counts explicit ?refresh=1 in the S5 budget - eviction-triggered re-fetch accounting is unstated.
findings.remediation_hint: State explicitly that a cache-miss-after-eviction re-download is a normal S5-budgeted request (not a TTL violation), and log it distinctly from refresh=1.

findings.finding: The owner's minimum checklist lists 'Retry-After' as a separate fixture; S9.2 merges it into the 418 fixture ('HTTP 418 with Retry-After + banned until body'). Parsing variants (header-only, body-only, neither) are covered in S12 unit tests, but no standalone Retry-After-only injection (e.g. 429 or 5xx with header, no banned-until body) exists in the checklist.
findings.remediation_hint: Add a Retry-After-only fixture (header without banned-until body) to the S9.2 checklist.

findings.finding: The 190-symbol MVP cap (one connection) rests on the stated venue combined-stream limit of 200/connection - a vendor-stated constant, not a measured one (Q-8: measured beats stated).
findings.remediation_hint: Verify the combined-stream limit with a live probe during implementation or keep the 10-symbol margin documented as the mitigation; record the measurement in G1 evidence.

summary: AUTHORIZED_WITH_FINDINGS: 0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH / 5 MEDIUM / 6 LOW. The plan is a faithful, law-compliant pre-registration for a platform cycle: worktree/branch/registry/A1-A7 discipline correct, owner test list fully covered, GO phrase exact, cutover + rollback + fail-closed law sound, and every hard stop present. Evidence claims verified against live bytes: 45/22 blocked-mark counts were exact at plan-commit instant (now 47/24, +2 loops), aiohttp/websockets/fastapi/uvicorn claim exact, both ACTIVE_LIGHT registries and all three worker pids alive, PacedFetch/bounded-retry code citations real (ops commit 99e00263 corroborates the 418 ban episode). The five MEDIUM findings are text-level remediations for A1: (1) the dual-run canary's direct-Binance leg sits outside every limiter on an already-banned shared egress IP; (2) non-retryable 4xx such as the now-live 403 are unclassified in the breaker law; (3) the 5xx branch does not honor Retry-After, which the owner hard stop requires unconditionally; (4) per-surface (7-state) vs per-datum (6-state) status vocabularies lack a mapping; (5) the 'first ~03:55Z' ledger claim is true only for ILLIQ (XSECT has blocked marks from 2026-09-15T16:30Z). Remediate the MEDIUMs in a plan amendment, then proceed to registration; no structural blocker found.
